dedupe_keys.name: particle dataset for constructing mineral processing case studies hzdr helmholtz institute freiberg

description: This RODARE record gives a training and a test set of mineral particles, measured with a mineral liberation analyser at the Helmholtz Institute Freiberg for Resource Technology, for building fictional mineral processing studies at particle level with known equations for different separation methods. The page says the probabilities and classes included with the data belong to a paper in the Journal of Cleaner Production and can be removed to build new cases; subjects are particle tracking, geometallurgy, mineral processing modelling, flotation, resource efficiency and automated mineralogy. It was published on 19 May 2020 by Lucas Pereira, Max Frenzel, Mahdi Khodadadzadeh, Raimon Tolosana Delgado and Jens Gutzmer as one downloadable Excel workbook of about 14 MB, free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is laboratory samples; the ore type and deposit are not stated on the page read. Caveats: the cases are constructed, not plant data, and the particle attributes and row counts are not stated on the page read. For simulation it supports particle-based models of concentrator circuits, testing how feed changes move recovery, energy use and tailings output of a processing plant, and benchmarking geometallurgical machine-learning models. Related catalogue records include the Brightway life cycle assessment framework, the global database of tailings flows and the USGS Mineral Resources Data System.
